question: Why Does My Premium Plugin Say Its License Key Is Invalid?
metaDescription: A domain mismatch after a migration, an expired subscription, or the site simply exceeding its license's activation limit are the usual reasons.
shortAnswer: Premium plugin licenses are typically tied to a specific domain and a limited number of simultaneous activations, so this message usually means one of those conditions changed — the site moved to a new domain without deactivating and reactivating the license there, the underlying subscription lapsed or was cancelled, or the license's activation limit was already used up on other sites (staging copies included, if not properly excluded).

bodyHtml:
Why This Happens

Most premium WordPress/WooCommerce plugin vendors validate licenses against a specific domain and cap how many sites can be simultaneously active under one license, both to enforce their pricing tiers and prevent unauthorized sharing. Anything that changes the domain, the subscription's active status, or the count of currently activated sites can trigger an invalid-license response, even for a legitimately purchased license.

Common Causes

  • A domain change (migration to a new domain, or even switching between staging and live URLs in some vendor implementations) without deactivating the license on the old domain and reactivating on the new one.
  • An expired or cancelled subscription, if the plugin is sold on a recurring license model rather than a one-time purchase — worth checking the account on the vendor's own site directly.
  • The license's activation limit already reached, commonly from staging copies, old development sites, or a previous domain that was never properly deactivated, quietly consuming activation slots.
  • A temporary vendor-side licensing server outage, less common but possible, worth checking the vendor's status page or support channels if everything else looks correct.

How to Fix It

  1. Log into the vendor's account portal directly to check the license's actual status, active domains, and remaining activation slots.
  2. Deactivate the license on any old or unused domains (a previous site, an old staging copy) to free up activation slots.
  3. Confirm the subscription is current if the plugin uses recurring licensing.
  4. Reactivate the license on the correct current domain from within the plugin's own settings once the above is confirmed clean.

Need help managing licenses across multiple environments? See WooCommerce fixes.
